parser.name: agent-manual
parser.recipe: 115-page born-digital catalog with a clean text layer (no OCR needed, unlike NAS1151-1158). A whole-document search for 'MS1410' located the two MS14101/MS14104 (narrow) and MS14102/MS14103 (wide) spherical-bearing spec pages; the DIMENSIONS -- TOLERANCES tables on pages 21 and 22 were read with --pattern and confirmed against a rendered crop of each table (the per-column tolerance is printed ONCE, in the table header row above the dash-number rows, and applies to every dash number in that column -- easy to miss with a text-only sweep, so both crops were checked visually before recording any tolerance).

document_meta.arrived_in_the_pile: Already in the pile before this session (verified on disk 2026-09-10); Jeff pointed to it by name for MS14101/MS14103 (handoff endstop_piece_part_acquisition's HITL ask) rather than dropping a new file in -- the two MS numbers are catalog sections inside this existing RBC document, not standalone MS spec sheets. A duplicate, apparently-identical copy also sits in the pile as 'RBC - Plain bearings (NAS77 p92).pdf'; this event cites the more complete '...Web.pdf' copy (its page 22 is present; the other copy's page 22 was not checked page-for-page beyond the MS1410x hits both share on page 9's index).

entries.subject: MS14101
entries.note: MS14104 & MS14101 SELF-LUBRICATED SPHERICAL BEARING, NARROW (chamfered/grooved pair on the same dash-number row; MS14104 is the chamfered variant, MS14101 the grooved variant -- 212956-005-A's parts list calls out the MS14101 dash, so this event's part_number entry below is the grooved column). Per-column tolerances apply to every dash number in the DIMENSIONS -- TOLERANCES table (printed once, in the header, not restated per row).

material.text: Outer ring: CRES 17-4PH, AMS 5643, HRC 28 min. Inner ring: CRES 440C, AMS 5630, HRC 55 min. Liner: Fibriloid® or “E” Uniflon® qualified to AS81820.

bore_tolerance_B.text: Column B (bore): +.0000 in / -.0005 in = +.000 mm / -.013 mm, printed once in the table header and applying to every dash number.
bore_tolerance_B.note: THE FACT THIS EVENT WAS ACQUIRED FOR (WORKSHEET_endstop_vision_baseline.md rows 34/36/50/54/56, 'pitch/tan link bearing size', GT 0.013 mm each). A unilateral band (nominal to -0.013 mm), total width 0.013 mm -- exact match to the workbook figure, confirmed by a rendered crop of the header row (the tolerance is easy to miss reading dash rows alone, since it is not repeated per row). The per-dash numeric value is on the MS14101-3 subject below.

od_tolerance_D.text: Column D (OD): +.0000 in / -.0005 in = +.000 mm / -.013 mm, same header convention as B.

entries.subject: MS14101-3
entries.note: The .1900 in bore dash. 212956-005-A.pdf's parts list calls out this dash as one of its two spherical bearings, identified by its bore ('.1900 BORE ID', WORKSHEET_endstop_vision_baseline.md §8a) -- the piece-part drawing for the bearing's own housing (213863-004, this same handoff) carries the mating bore, not this bearing's own tolerance.

bore_B.text: .1900 in / 4.826 mm, -0.013 mm per the family's bore_tolerance_B.

od_D.text: .5625 in / 14.288 mm, -0.013 mm per the family's od_tolerance_D.
od_D.note: Coincidentally the same 14.288 mm figure as MS9363-09's nut_height and NAS6403U11D's family -- unrelated parts; not a cross-reference, just a shared basic in./mm conversion (.5625 in).

width_H.text: .281 in / 7.14 mm. Band ±.005 in / ±.13 mm, per the family table header (not restated per dash).

ball_width_W.text: .218 in / 5.54 mm. Band +.000/-.002 in = +.00/-.05 mm, per the family table header.

entries.subject: MS14103
entries.note: MS14102 & MS14103 SELF-LUBRICATED SPHERICAL BEARING, WIDE (chamfered/grooved pair; MS14102 chamfered, MS14103 grooved -- 212956-005-A's parts list calls out the MS14103 dash, so the part_number entry below is the grooved column). Same AS81820 standard, material and temperature range as MS14101; the wide series differs from the narrow series only in width/OD-family geometry, not in the bore-tolerance convention.

material.text: Outer ring: CRES 17-4PH, AMS 5643, HRC 28 min. Inner ring: CRES 440C, AMS 5630, HRC 55 min. Liner: Fibriloid® or “E” Uniflon® qualified to AS81820.

bore_tolerance_B.text: Column B (bore): +.0000 in / -.0005 in = +.000 mm / -.013 mm, printed once in the table header and applying to every dash number -- IDENTICAL convention and value to MS14101's bore_tolerance_B, confirmed by an independent crop of this (wide-series) table.
bore_tolerance_B.note: THE FACT THIS EVENT WAS ACQUIRED FOR (WORKSHEET_endstop_vision_baseline.md rows 34/36/50/54/56, GT 0.013 mm each) -- same match as MS14101's. The per-dash numeric value is on the MS14103-3 subject below.

entries.subject: MS14103-3
entries.note: The .1900 in bore dash -- same bore as MS14101-3, wider body. 212956-005-A.pdf's parts list calls out this dash as the SECOND of its two spherical bearings.

bore_B.text: .1900 in / 4.826 mm, -0.013 mm per the family's bore_tolerance_B -- identical bore to MS14101-3.

od_D.text: .6250 in / 15.875 mm, -0.013 mm per the family's od_tolerance_D. Wider than MS14101-3's OD (14.288 mm) at the same bore -- the 'wide' series name describes the outer geometry, not the bore.

width_H.text: .327 in / 8.31 mm. Band ±.005 in / ±.13 mm, per the family table header.

ball_width_W.text: .437 in / 11.10 mm. Band +.000/-.002 in = +.00/-.05 mm, per the family table header.

notes: Do not confuse these metal self-aligning spherical bearings (MS14101-3/MS14103-3, AS81820) with the Trelleborg Turcon Slydring polymer piston/rod bearing family (event 0005) -- a prior session's note already flags this, and this event does not change it.

Only pages 21-22 (the MS14101/MS14104 narrow and MS14102/MS14103 wide spherical-bearing sections) were read. This is a 115-page catalog covering rod-end bearings, journal bearings and links/assemblies as well; no claim is made about the rest of it.

The catalog's DIMENSIONS — TOLERANCES tables print the per-column tolerance ONCE, in the header row above the first dash-number row, rather than repeating it on every row -- confirmed by rendering both tables as images (a text-only sweep sees the header tolerance and the dash-row values as separate, unlabelled hits and could miss which one applies to which). Every dash row in both tables uses that same header tolerance; nothing dash-specific overrides it for -3.
